findings.evidence: exports.def:6 adds 'QueueHudPerformCastSpell'; kotor2-steam-aspyr.hooks.toml:31 binds the H10 detour to function = "QueueHudPerformCastSpell". A Grep of the whole queue_hud_src directory finds the name only in those two files; no definition exists in QueueHud.cpp or any other source. Known facts: build_check FAIL rc=1 with 'collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status'.
findings.suggested_investigation: Grep patch_manager_mods/queue_hud_src for 'QueueHudPerformCastSpell' and for any extern "C" definition of it. Confirm the link error names this symbol by re-running the queue_hud_src build in the scratch copy (not the live game directory). Then check that the definition's signature matches the hook: int __cdecl taking (int clientCreature, int ebp), with a non-zero return meaning 'consumed', as QueueHudPerformUseItem does at QueueHud.cpp:871.
findings.why_it_matters: The export and the hook target have no implementation, so the DLL cannot link (the packet's build gate fails hard). If a stub were linked instead, the H10 detour at 0x00775703 would route game execution into an undefined or wrong handler. Under the Gate Invariant, the rebuilt .kpatch cannot pass and cannot be installed until the handler exists.

findings.evidence: Lines 26-27 claim '6 bytes (2 instructions): SUB ESP,0x0C / MOV [EBP-0x0C],ECX' and 'Non-zero return jumps to 0x77574C (MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP / RET 0x1C)'. Line 32: original_bytes = [0x83, 0xEC, 0x0C, 0x89, 0x4D, 0xF4]; line 33: consumed_exit_address = 0x0077574C. The bytes decode correctly (83 EC 0C = SUB ESP,0xC; 89 4D F4 = MOV [EBP-0xC],ECX; both whole instructions with no relative operands), but 0x0077574C and 'RET 0x1C' are not backed by any source in the packet.
findings.suggested_investigation: Disassemble the vanilla exe (read-only, from the vanilla copy, not the live install) at 0x00775703 and 0x0077574C. Confirm the 6 bytes match, the instruction at 0x00775709 is a whole-instruction boundary, and the epilogue at 0x0077574C is MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP / RET imm16 with the imm16 that the comment states. Confirm PerformCastSpell's argument byte count against its callers.
findings.why_it_matters: The consumed exit must be an instruction boundary that restores ESP/EBP and returns with the callee's correct stack cleanup. A wrong RET n corrupts the caller's stack on every consumed cast. The address is 0x43 past the hook, and the only comparison available is the H9 entry, which uses RET 0x10 for a different function, so the value is unverified.

findings.evidence: QueueHud.cpp:532: 'if (!guikit::getExtent(hud + 0x6594, &bg.x, &bg.y, &bg.w, &bg.h) || bg.w <= 0 || bg.h <= 0) { bg = qh::combatBgRect(q0); }'. The only other HUD offsets in the file are named constants (HudSlotBase = 0x5F2C at line 62, HudSlotStride = 0x148). 0x6594 is an unnamed literal with no source comment, and it is read from the HUD struct on every frame of the combat background draw.
findings.suggested_investigation: Find the engine source for the 0x6594 control offset (the symbol lookup the raw-address rule requires) and add a named constant with a comment citing it. If there is no source, check whether hud+0x6594 is the same control as one of the HudSlotBase slots, and check whether getExtent validates the pointer through saferead before use.
findings.why_it_matters: An invented offset read through a raw HUD pointer can return an extent from an unrelated control. The fallback hides the failure, so the background is drawn in the wrong place with no log. Nothing in the packet shows where 0x6594 comes from.

notes: Scanner triage: S-e5dafaa321 and S-fa34e6564b are H9 (0x775603 = decimal 7820803) and H10 (0x775703 = decimal 7821059), not H8 as the labels suggest. Their original_bytes and consumed exits match the file text. S-23ca8725d4, S-50997bab0d and S-679b1dcb74 are parser artifacts from the [[hooks.parameters]] tables and are harmless. Pointer-math hits S-0d80b5c9f3, S-33c8105540, S-477a37c516, S-5d43a24edd, S-922fc54a97 and S-923dcf5c6e are uintptr-to-void* casts on 32-bit values, each preceded by a saferead probe in tickItemQueues; I found nothing wrong with them. Not checked: the parity of H8's removal (no GOG hooks file is in the packet), the QueueHud.cpp uses of cancel(), userCancelled and ItemBuffer, and the binary itself (no vanilla exe reads). The 'depends_on_live_install' fact means nothing here reads the live patch_config.toml, so the checker runs are scratch-only. Build failure is the packet's blocking item: a passing run_tests does not cover the link failure.
